scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: CONTINUATION PATTERNS: SYMMETRICAL, ASCENDING & DESCENDING TRIANGLES

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. The Symmetrical Triangle (Coil). A neutral continuation pattern formed by two converging trendlines: lower highs and higher lows converging toward an apex; requires at least four reversal points.
beats.en_subtitle: Pillar one: 1. The Symmetrical Triangle (Coil). A neutral continuation pattern formed by two converging trendlines: lower highs and higher lows converging toward an apex; requires at least four reversal points.

cards.title: 1. The Symmetrical Triangle (Coil)
cards.desc: A neutral continuation pattern formed by two converging trendlines: lower highs and higher lows converging toward an apex; requires at least four reversal points.

cards.title: 2. The Ascending Triangle (Bullish)
cards.desc: Features a flat horizontal upper resistance ceiling and a rising lower support trendline, signaling that buyers are increasingly aggressive.

cards.title: 3. The Descending Triangle (Bearish)
cards.desc: Features a flat horizontal lower support floor and a declining upper resistance trendline, signaling persistent institutional distribution.

cards.title: 4. The Apex Time Limit Rule
cards.desc: Breakouts must occur between two-thirds (66%) and three-quarters (75%) of the horizontal pattern width; breakouts near the apex lose technical authority.

ui_state.question: A stock in an established uptrend forms a bullish ascending triangle with a flat horizontal upper resistance ceiling at ₹300 and a rising lower trendline. The widest vertical base of the triangle measures ₹50. The stock then breaks decisively above ₹300 on expanding volume at the two-thirds point of the pattern. What is the minimum price objective?
options: A) ₹325 (half of the pattern base)
B) ₹350 (adding the ₹50 vertical base height to the ₹300 breakout level)
C) ₹300 (the breakout point itself)
D) Triangles cannot project vertical price targets.
ui_state.answer: B) Under Murphy's triangle measuring rule: Target = Breakout Level (₹300) + Base Height (₹50) = ₹350.00.

steps: 1. Triangles are continuation patterns: trade in the direction of the trend preceding pattern entry.
2. A valid triangle requires at least four reversal points: two highs and two lows touching the trendlines.
3. Trading volume must contract noticeably as price coils tighter toward the triangle apex.
4. The breakout must occur between two-thirds and three-quarters of the pattern width for maximum momentum.
5. If price reaches the final quarter toward the apex without breaking out, the pattern loses technical power.
6. Ascending triangles are inherently bullish; descending triangles are inherently bearish.
7. Valid upside breakouts require a decisive closing penetration accompanied by an unmistakable volume surge.
8. Minimum target: measure the widest vertical base height and project it from the breakout level.
